name: Mueller Hut Route
why: About 1,000 m straight up from the village to the hut on the Sealy Range, facing the hanging glaciers and ice cliffs of Mount Sefton above the Mueller Glacier.
book: As a day walk: free. Register your intentions at the Aoraki/Mount Cook Visitor Centre the day you start and sign out after. To sleep at Mueller Hut, book it (mid-November to 30 April). Parking at White Horse Hill costs $25 a day.
water: Carry all your water for the day; the hut tap water is untreated: boil it.
dangers: Above Sealy Tarns it is an unmaintained alpine route over rock and a loose scree slope: follow the orange poles and always see the next one.
Snow and ice from March to November; avalanche danger from April to mid-November. Then it needs ice axe, crampons and avalanche gear.
Fast weather changes, strong wind and low visibility on the ridge.
Ice is common on the lower ridge in the morning: wait for it to soften before descending.
turnaround: Sealy Tarns is the decision point (DOC): if the weather is closing in, someone is struggling or you cannot reach the hut with time to spare, go back down from there.

points.name: Aoraki/Mount Cook Village
points.note: Follow the Kea Point Track from the village, then the Sealy Tarns Track, steps most of the way.

points.name: Sealy Tarns
points.note: Small tarns on a shelf, 2 hours up, with Aoraki and the Hooker Valley behind you. The decision point.

points.name: Mueller Hut
points.note: 1,800 m, under Mount Ollivier, the first peak Edmund Hillary climbed. The Mueller Glacier and Mount Sefton's ice shelf across the valley.
